title: World religions
description: The core beliefs, texts and practices of five major religions, described plainly.

ideas.title: Judaism
ideas.summary: Judaism centers on one God, the covenant with the people of Israel, and a life shaped by the Torah.

items.q: What is the Torah, in Judaism?
items.a: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible, the foundation of Jewish law and teaching

items.q: What is the Jewish day of rest, kept from Friday evening to Saturday evening?
Which Jewish festival recalls the Exodus, the deliverance of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt?
Which day is the holiest of the Jewish year, a day of fasting and atonement?
items.a: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement

ideas.title: Christianity
ideas.summary: Christians hold that Jesus of Nazareth is the Christ, the Son of God, whose death and resurrection bring salvation.

items.q: What name is given to the four accounts of the life of Jesus that open the New Testament?
items.a: The Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke and John)

items.q: Which Christian feast celebrates the resurrection of Jesus?
What is the Christian doctrine that one God exists as Father, Son and Holy Spirit called?
What are the three main branches of Christianity?

ideas.title: Islam
ideas.summary: Muslims worship one God and follow the Qur'an, which they hold was revealed to the prophet Muhammad.

items.q: What is the holy book of Islam, and to whom do Muslims believe it was revealed?
items.a: The Qur'an, revealed to the prophet Muhammad

items.q: What is the shahada, the first of the Five Pillars of Islam?
items.a: The profession of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is his messenger

items.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims fast from dawn to sunset?
To which city do Muslims make the pilgrimage called the hajj?
What are the two largest branches of Islam?

ideas.title: Hinduism
ideas.summary: Hinduism is a family of traditions sharing ideas of dharma, karma and rebirth, with the Vedas as its oldest scriptures.

items.q: In Hindu thought, what is karma?
items.a: The principle that a person's actions bring fitting consequences, in this life or a later one

items.q: What do Hindus and Buddhists call the cycle of birth, death and rebirth?
In Hinduism, what is moksha?
items.a: Release from the cycle of rebirth

items.q: What are the oldest scriptures of Hinduism called?

ideas.title: Buddhism
ideas.summary: The Buddha taught that suffering arises from craving and can be ended by following the Eightfold Path.

items.q: Who was the founder of Buddhism, known as the Buddha?
What is the first of the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism?
What is the Buddhist path to the end of suffering called?
In Buddhism, what is nirvana?
items.a: The end of craving and suffering, and release from the cycle of rebirth

ideas.title: Families of faith
ideas.summary: Judaism, Christianity and Islam trace themselves to Abraham; Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism arose in India.

items.q: Which three religions are called Abrahamic because they trace their origins to Abraham?
What is the term for belief in one God?
Which religion was founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab around 1500?
